{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-9098.44","title":"radio.py: 9098.39 GE shim wipes burst state every apply","description":"## Problem

9098.39 stopped stash from walking every neighbor on one `(source, tx.id)` Gilbert-Elliott machine by applying a shim with a fresh `_link_states={}` per receiver:

```python
shim = replace(rule, _link_states={})
shim._lichen_rx_id = rx_node_id  # never read by GilbertElliottRule.apply
return shim.apply(candidate, rx_position)
```

`GilbertElliottRule` documents a two-state Markov chain **per link** that updates on each unique transmission (`lora_medium/chaos.py`: "link A→B can be in a fading burst while A→C operates normally"; average burst length `1/p_bad_to_good` packets). `apply()` still keys by `(source, tx.id)` and ignores dest / `_lichen_rx_id`. The empty shim means:

1. Every radio.py apply starts in Good. Good→Bad never survives to the next `tx.id`.
2. The original `rule._link_states` is never written. `test_ge_two_receivers_independent_of_add_order` asserts `ge._link_states == {}`, locking the wipe.
3. `_lichen_rx_id` is dead: dest is not bound. Independence is only "new empty machine + shared rng", not a per-(src, dst) chain.

Through radio.py, GE is independent Bernoulli-with-a-first-transition, not a burst process. `test_chaos.py` `test_gilbert_elliott_always_bad_state_loses_all` / `test_gilbert_elliott_burst_pattern` call `rule.apply` directly and still see memory; mesh/HIL/metrics paths do not.

With default-ish GE (`p_good_to_bad=0.02`, `p_bad_to_good=0.3`, `loss_prob_bad=0.6`), long-run loss is similar but clustering is gone. OSCORE/replay/partition tests under "burst RF" measure i.i.d. loss. `_drop_chaos_state_for_tx` at TxEnd also drops `_ge_survived`, so even a radio-side cache cannot carry Bad into the next packet.

This is not 9098.39 (intra-TX neighbor chaining on one `(source, tx.id)` key). 9098.39 option (2) was persist per `(source, dest)`. The empty shim implemented option (1) too literally.

## Why this is security (fault-injection oracle)

GE is the burst-RF oracle for mesh security and capacity. A 500-node / city-mesh run with GE must produce temporally correlated drops on a link. Radio.py makes every packet a new Good-state draw. Seeded A/B (`compare_metrics`) of hopping/OSCORE-under-burst is not the documented channel model. `test_radio.py` GE cases are single-TX (`tx`+`rx` or two RX of one TX) so the wipe is invisible.

## Files

- `python/src/lichen/sim/simulation/radio.py` (`_apply_ge_independent`, `_drop_chaos_state_for_tx` at TxEnd)
- `python/tests/sim/test_radio.py` (`test_ge_two_receivers_independent_of_add_order` asserts empty `_link_states`; no two-TX burst oracle)
